newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-SRI LANKA STRIKE TWO EARLY BLOWS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKA STRIKE TWO EARLY BLOWS.

text.p: Sri Lanka captured two early wickets to put India under pressure at lunch on the second day of the second and final test on Sunday.
India, facing Sri Lanka's first innings total of 332 all out, were 39 for two at the interval, with opener Navjot Sidhu and captain Sachin Tendulkar fending off the home side's new ball attack.
Chaminda Vaas struck an early blow for Sri Lanka when he forced Ajay Jadeja to edge a catch to wicketkeeper Romesh Kaluwitharana for one when the total was only two.
Sajeeva de Silva, the other left-arm seamer in the side, sent back Rahul Dravid for two when the batmsan hooked a short delivery down to Vaas at long leg.
Earlier Sri Lanka added only 16 to their overnight 316 for seven as debutant Debasis Mohanty took two more wickets to finish with four for 78.
He sent back Aravinda de Silva and Ravindra Pushpakumara to wrap up the innings.
De Silva made 146, batting for 365 minutes, facing 228 balls and hit 20 fours in compiling his 13th test century.
